# Part 1: Population Structure

```{r plotcols}
#sampling area

levels(popdata$area)
```

## 1.1 PCA with pcadapt
*requires .bed format*    

packages required
```{r part4.1pkg}
library(pcadapt)
```

read in bed file
```{r bedfile}
SLF_bed <- read.pcadapt("Final.SLF.bed", type = "bed") 

#specify populations -- order is by population 
popbed <- popdata[,c("fly_ID","area")] #just population identity
poplist.names <- popbed[,2] #just population list
```

Preliminary determination of PCs to retain
```{r prelimPCA, warning=FALSE}
x <- pcadapt(input = SLF_bed, K = 5)  #use large number of K  to start

pdf("scree_plot.K20.pdf")
scree <- plot(x, option = "screeplot") 
dev.off()

# Call your plotting commands,# no clear clustering
plot(x, option = "scores", pop = poplist.names)

# Compute the total variance
total_variance <- sum(x$singular.values^2)

# Compute the percentage of variance explained by each PC
percentage_variance <- (x$singular.values^2) / total_variance * 100

# Print the percentage of variance explained by each PC, each PC explain litte variance
print(percentage_variance)

```

visualize PC variation to determine how many PC to retain
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Convert the scores to a data frame and add population names
x2df <- data.frame(x$scores)
x2df$pops <- as.factor(poplist.names)  # Ensure the population names are treated as a factor

# Create the plot for the first two principal components
PC12 <- ggplot(x2df, aes(x=X1, y=X2, color=pops)) +  # Ensure column names are correctly referenced
  geom_point(cex=2) +  # Size of the points
  theme_bw() +  # White background theme
  scale_color_manual(values=location_colors) +  # Use the predefined location colors
  xlab("PC1") +  # Label for the x-axis
  ylab("PC2") +  # Label for the y-axis
  stat_ellipse(alpha=0.35) +  # Add ellipses to group points by population
  theme(legend.position="right")  # Position the legend on the right side

PC34 <-ggplot(x2df, aes(x=X3, y=X4, color=pops)) +  
  geom_point(cex=2) +  # Size of the points
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values=location_colors) + 
  xlab("PC3") +  # Label for the x-axis
  ylab("PC4") +  # Label for the y-axis
  stat_ellipse(alpha=0.35) +  
  theme(legend.position="right")  

print(PC12)
print(PC34)

ggsave(filename = "PC12.pdf", plot = PC12)
ggsave(filename = "PC34.pdf", plot = PC34)
```

# Part 2 : DAPC(Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components)
This multivariate approach allows for the exploration of genetic variation by constructing synthetic variables from linear combinations of alleles, where these variables are designed to capture the essence of genetic diversity among individuals. 

Run DAPC with adegenet, run the job below on hpc, it's memory demanding.
Do not run in R markdown.
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(adegenet)
library(vcfR)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(0314)

# Read the VCF file
vcf <- read.vcfR("/Users/fallonmong/Documents/Documents - Fallon MacBook Pro/FallonPaper Old/10KB.maf0.01.missing0.9.id0.2.vcf")

location_colors <- c("Bronx" = "#252525", 
                     "Brooklyn" =  "#e6ab02",
                     "Camden, NJ" = "#a65628",
                     "Connecticut" = "#e41a1c" ,
                     "Governor Island" = "#08589e",
                     "Manhattan" = "#c861a5",
                     "Staten island" = "#3690c0",
                     "West Orange, NJ" = "#009E73")

popdata <- read.csv("2022 SLF Info new.csv", header=T) 
#link populations
popgen_sort <- popdata[order(popdata$fly_ID),c("fly_ID","area")] 
#ordered and reduced to just columns we need

# Convert VCF to genlight object
slf.gen = vcfR2genlight(vcf)

#assigns the 'area' column of the sorted dataframe to the 'pop' slot of the genlight object.
pop(slf.gen) <- popgen_sort[,2] #assign populations to gen file
slf.gen@pop #verify population attribute

#find cluster
clusters_result <- find.clusters(slf.gen,parallel = require("parallel"), n.cores=8)

SLF_dapc <- dapc(slf.gen, clusters_result$grp)

scatter(SLF_dapc, posi.da="bottomleft")

# cross-validation for the DAPC 
optx_slf <- xvalDapc(tab(slf.gen, NA.method = "mean"), pop(slf.gen), parallel="multicore", ncpus=8L)  
#look for leveling off window
optx_slf[2:7]

```

Run DAPC after cross-validation and visualize DAPC, run it on hpc
```{r}
#run DAPC with the recommendation of Cross Validataion
dapc.allsamples35 <- dapc(slf.gen,  n.pca=35, n.da=7, var.contrib=T, scale=F,parallel = require("parallel"), n.cores=12)

#visualize DAPC
# Set up a PDF device
pdf("withlabel.New.SLF.PC35.da7.allsamples.png")
# Plot the DAPC scatter plot
scatter(dapc.allsamples35, clabel=0.9, col=location_colors,
        scree.pca=FALSE, scree.da =FALSE, cell=1.5, cex=1, mstree=FALSE)  # retain 2 df
# Turn off the device
dev.off()

```

```{r}
# Read the sample meta dataset
popdata <- read.csv("2022 SLF Info new.csv", header = TRUE)

# Read the sample meta dataset
popdata <- read.csv("2022 SLF Info new.csv", header = TRUE)

# Convert 'area' to a factor
popdata$area <- as.factor(popdata$area)

location_colors <- c("Bronx" = "#beaed4",
                     "Brooklyn" = "#e6ab02",
                     "Camden, NJ" = "#a65628",
                     "Connecticut" = "#e41a1c",
                     "Governor Island" = "#08589e",
                     "Manhattan" = "#c861a5",
                     "Staten island" = "#3690c0",
                     "West Orange, NJ" = "#009E73")

# Read the tree file
treefile <- read.tree("Final.SNPTree.treefile")

# Ensure the tree tip labels match with IDs in popdata
treefile$tip.label <- as.character(popdata$fly_ID)

# Map each tip label to its area based on popdata
tip_areas <- popdata$area[match(treefile$tip.label, popdata$fly_ID)]

# Match the areas to the colors defined in location_colors
tip_colors <- location_colors[as.character(tip_areas)]

# Function to assign colors to internal branches based on the majority color of descendant tips
assign_branch_colors <- function(tree, tip_colors) {
  num_edges <- nrow(tree$edge)
  branch_colors <- rep("black", num_edges)
  
  for (i in 1:num_edges) {
    node <- tree$edge[i, 2]
    if (node <= length(tip_colors)) {
      branch_colors[i] <- tip_colors[node]
    } else {
      descendant_tips <- which(tree$edge[, 1] == node)
      descendant_colors <- branch_colors[descendant_tips]
      branch_colors[i] <- names(which.max(table(descendant_colors)))
    }
  }
  
  return(branch_colors)
}

# Assign colors to the branches based on the majority color of descendant tips
branch_colors <- assign_branch_colors(treefile, tip_colors)

pdf("unrootted_phylogenetic_tree_plot.pdf")

# Plot the unrooted tree with branch colors and no tip labels
ape::plot.phylo(x = treefile, type = "unrooted", edge.color = branch_colors, show.tip.label = FALSE)
# Add a legend for the area colors
legend("bottomright", legend = names(location_colors), fill = location_colors, title = "Area", cex = 0.8)

# Close the PNG device
dev.off()

# Create a vector of branch colors based on the tip colors
branch_colors <- rep("black", length(treefile$edge.length))
for (i in 1:length(treefile$tip.label)) {
  tip_index <- which(treefile$edge[, 2] == i)
  branch_colors[tip_index] <- tip_colors[i]
}

# Plot the unrooted tree with branch colors, no tip labels, and node labels
ape::plot.phylo(x = treefile, type = "unrooted", edge.color = branch_colors, show.tip.label = FALSE,  cex = 0.7)

# Add a legend for the area colors
legend("bottomright", legend = names(location_colors), fill = location_colors, title = "Area", cex = 0.8)
```

#Part 4: snmf with LEA
The snmf() function produces results similar to the widely-used computer program STRUCTURE.
The cross-entropy criterion is based on the prediction of a fraction of masked genotypes (matrix completion), and on the cross-validation approach. Smaller values of the cross-entropy criterion usually mean better runs. 

```{r}
library(LEA)
library(RColorBrewer)

#get population list
location_colors <- c("Bronx" = "#252525", 
                     "Brooklyn" =  "#e6ab02",
                     "Camden, NJ" = "#a65628",
                     "Connecticut" = "#e41a1c" ,
                     "Governor Island" = "#08589e",
                     "Manhattan" = "#c861a5",
                     "Staten island" = "#3690c0",
                     "West Orange, NJ" = "#009E73")

popdata <- read.csv("2022 SLF Info new.csv", header=T)
popbed <- popdata[,c("fly_ID","area")]
poplist.names <- popbed[,2]

#read the data in ped format
SLF_geno <- ped2geno("Final.SLF.vcf.ped") 

#run snmf, starting with large number of K
Final_slf_snmf <- snmf(SLF_geno,
                   K = 1:10, entropy = TRUE, project = "new",alpha=100,
                   repetitions = 10, ploidy = 2)

# Open a PDF device
pdf("cross_entropy_plot.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)

# Create the plot
plot(Final_slf_snmf, col = "blue", pch = 19, cex = 1.2)

# Close the PDF device
dev.off()

#needs entropy=T in snmf Cross-entropy quantifies how well the probability distribution q predicts p. A smaller cross-entropy indicates that q is a better approximation of p.
entropy=sapply(1:10,FUN=function(i)
cross.entropy(Final_slf_snmf,K = i))

ce <-  cross.entropy(Final_slf_snmf, K = 4)
ce
# select the run with the lowest cross-entropy for K = 3
best_run <- which.min(ce)

```

plot for snmf for different areas
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)

# define the color
#get population list
location_colors <- c("Bronx" = "#252525", 
                     "Brooklyn" =  "#e6ab02",
                     "Camden, NJ" = "#a65628",
                     "Connecticut" = "#e41a1c" ,
                     "Governor Island" = "#08589e",
                     "Manhattan" = "#c861a5",
                     "Staten island" = "#3690c0",
                     "West Orange, NJ" = "#009E73")

plotcolors <- c("#e6ab02","#a65628","#e41a1c","#08589e","#c861a5","#3690c0","#009E73","#252525")

# Loop for K = 2 to K = 10
for (K in 3:5) {
    ce <- cross.entropy(Final_slf_snmf, K = K)
    best_run <- which.min(ce)
    tbl <- Q(Final_slf_snmf, K = K, run = best_run)
    colnames(tbl) <- paste0("P", 1:K)
    
    # Convert to data frame and process
    q_df <- as_tibble(tbl) %>% 
            mutate(individual = popbed$fly_ID, region = popbed$area)
    
    q_df_long <- q_df %>%
        gather(ancestry, proportion, paste0("P", 1:K)) %>%
        arrange(region, individual)
    
    q_df_ordered <- q_df_long %>%
        group_by(region, individual) %>%
        mutate(likely_assignment = ancestry[which.max(proportion)],
               assignment_prob = max(proportion)) %>%
        arrange(region, likely_assignment, desc(assignment_prob)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(individual = forcats::fct_inorder(factor(individual)))
    
    # Plot
    plot <- ggplot(q_df_ordered, aes(x = interaction(region, individual, sep = "_"), y = proportion, fill = ancestry)) +
            geom_col() +
            scale_fill_manual(values = plotcolors[1:K]) +
            labs(fill = "Ancestry") +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
                  axis.line = element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8), 
                  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = "black"),
                  panel.background = element_blank(),
                  axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
                  panel.grid = element_blank()) +
            xlab("Region_Individual") +
            ylab("Proportion")
    
    # Save the plot to a PDF file
    pdf_file <- paste0("AncestryPlot_K", K, ".pdf")
    ggsave(pdf_file, plot, width = 11, height = 8.5, device = "pdf")
}

```

# Part 5: Admixture
Run it on hpc, I ran K1 to 10 with 10 indepent replicates
```{r}
# Choose the best K
#Use ADMIXTURE’s cross-validation procedure. A good value of K will exhibit a low cross-validation error compared to other K values. 
setwd("/scratch/fm2371/Winchell/SLF_spring23/SLF_spring23/raw.vcf/Final/Admixture")

# Read in the data
data <- list.files(pattern = "Final\\.log.*\\.out", full.names = TRUE)

# Use lapply to read in all log files at once
bigData <- lapply(data, readLines)

# Find the line that starts with "CV error"
library(stringr)
foundset_cv <- sapply(bigData, function(x) x[which(str_detect(x, "^CV error"))])

# Extract the numeric value from the "CV error" line
cv_errors <- as.numeric(sub("CV error \\(K=\\d+\\): (-?\\d+\\.\\d+).*", "\\1", foundset_cv))

# Create a data frame with K values and corresponding CV errors
cv_df <- data.frame(
  K = rep(1:10, each = 10),
  cv_error = cv_errors
)

# Calculate the mean CV error for each K
cv_summary <- aggregate(cv_error ~ K, data = cv_df, FUN = mean)

cv_summary_plot <- ggplot(cv_summary, aes(x = K, y = cv_error)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C3E50", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#E74C3C", size = 3) +
  #geom_text(aes(label = K), nudge_x = 0.2, nudge_y = 0.002, size = 4, color = "#2C3E50") +
  labs(x = "K", y = "Mean CV Error") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "cm")
  ) +
  ggtitle("Mean CV Error over 10 replicates") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, max(cv_summary$K), by = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(min(cv_summary$cv_error) - 0.005, max(cv_summary$cv_error) + 0.005))

ggsave(filename="cv_summary_plot.pdf", plot=cv_summary_plot, width=12, height=8, units="in")
ggsave(filename="cv_summary_plot.png", plot=cv_summary_plot,dpi = 300)
```

This indicates K=3 is the best.
```{r}
#plot for K3 to K8 
# Set the working directory
setwd("/Users/fallonmong/Documents/Documents - Fallon MacBook Pro/FallonPaper Final/Admixture")

# Assuming popdata is read before this snippet
#popdata <- read.csv("~/Documents/Documents - Fallon MacBook Pro/FallonPaper New/No_LD_Pruning/2022 SLF Info new.csv", header=T)
popbed <- popdata[,c("fly_ID","area")]

# Your custom colors
plotcolors <- c("#c861a5","#3690c0","#009E73","#e6ab02","#a65628","#08589e","#e41a1c","#252525")

# Loop over each K value
for (K in 3:8) {
  # File name based on K value
  file_name <- paste0("Final.", K, ".Q")
  
  # Read the data
  tbl <- read.table(file_name)
  
  # convert the q matrix to a data frame
  q_df <- tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(individual = popbed$fly_ID,
           region = popbed$area)
  
  # Convert the wide-form data to long-form
  q_df_long <- q_df %>%
    gather(ancestry, proportion, paste0("V", 1:K)) %>%
    arrange(region, individual)
  
  # Order the data by region, likely assignment, and assignment probability
  q_df_ordered <- q_df_long %>%
    group_by(region, individual) %>%
    mutate(likely_assignment = ancestry[which.max(proportion)],
           assignment_prob = max(proportion)) %>%
    arrange(region, likely_assignment, desc(assignment_prob)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(individual = forcats::fct_inorder(factor(individual)))
  
  # Plot the data
  plot <- q_df_ordered %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = interaction(region, individual, sep = "_"), y = proportion, fill = ancestry)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = plotcolors[1:K]) +
    labs(fill = "Ancestry") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
          axis.line = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = "black"),
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
          panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    xlab("Region_Individual") +
    ylab("Proportion")
  
  # Save the plot to a PDF file
  pdf_file <- paste0("AdmixturePlot_K", K, ".pdf")
  ggsave(pdf_file, plot, width = 14, height = 8, device = "pdf")
}
```

```{r}
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(individual = forcats::fct_inorder(factor(individual)))
```

```{r}
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  xlab("Individual") +
  ylab("Proportion") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(region), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

# Save the plot to a PDF file

# Save the plot to a PNG file
```
